chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Tommy Ladnier and Sam Wooding
summary: Cheatham rates Tommy Ladnier next to Louis, says Wooding disliked him, tells of Wooding underpaying him, and of rooming with Ladnier until he left in Nice.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about Tommy Ladnier -- Sam apparently did not think very much of him as a trumpet player.
He didn't. I don't know why, but I think Sam kept Tommy because of his name. I think that's about the only reason. Because Tom had been over there before with Sam.
I know, he was with him, originally.
Yes.
And Sam told me that he -- he really wanted Louie --
But I -- (inaudible). that's what I mean, see --
-- and Louie had gone with Fletcher
so he got Tommy instead.
Yes, because Tommy also replaced Louie in Fletcher's band.
Uh-huh.
And that was -- as far as Sam's concerned that was great jazz man. I don't know what happened to -- I don't know what happend, but I really rated Tommy up there next to Louie, I did.
Uh-huh.
At the time I heard him. I thought he was a great trumpet player and he was. Well Sam for some reason or other -- they didn't -- I don't think they got along too well.
Uh-huh.

Because Tommy was very independent type of man and he wouldn't stand for any foolishness, you know. Sam was taking -- you know, he had his way because he was underpaying me and I knew that's why I left him in Hamburg. I was doing all that playing, lead trumpet in the band and I learned that he was paying me so much under what he was paying the rest of the guys, I quit. Berlin, when he came and picked me up then he raised my salary. But Tommy I thought was one of the greatest trumpet players -- I could dig him because he had the New Orleans touch. And that's what I liked. I liked it. And Tommy and I roomed together, the whole time
we were in the band up until the time just before he left Sam in Nice. He left Sam in Nice.
You say he was a very independent man?

Oh, yes Tommy was very independent, and a good man. Very good hearted man. Tommy was a very jovial type of guy, full of fun all the time. I think the band kind of got on his nerves too, because I don't think he had an opportunity to play as much as he wanted to.
Uh-huh.
So, he wanted to get out -- get with someone where he could do more playing.
